previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A man with end-stage renal disease, type 1 diabetes, cardiomyopathy (multifactorial, including Chagas disease), and a history of coronary artery bypass grafting was admitted for lightheadedness and bradycardia. He was found to have severe hyperkalemia (K 8.0) with EKG changes including peaked T waves and conduction delays. He received emergency treatment with atropine, insulin, dextrose, calcium, and albuterol, followed by hemodialysis, which normalized his potassium and resolved the arrhythmia. His carvedilol, torsemide, and spironolactone were discontinued due to bradycardia and minimal urine output. He remained stable, with improving electrolytes and no recurrence of symptoms, and was discharged home with plans to follow up with cardiology for pacemaker evaluation and nephrology for dialysis management.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old man with h/o DM, ESRD on HD MWF, 
pancreatitis, gallstones, who presents with RUQ pain, N/V.  

#. Pancreatitis: The patient presented with pain, nausea, and 
vomiting similar to previous episodes of pancreatitis. In the 
ED, lipase levels were elevated indicative of an acute 
pancreatitis. He was seen by general surgery in the ED who 
determined that the source of the recurrent pancreatitis was 
most likely gallstones versus pancreatic divisum. The patient 
was started on IV fluids, anti-nausea, and pain medications and 
transferred to the floor. Over the course of ___ days, the 
patient's symptoms resolved and he was able to tolerate POs. 
When the symptoms had completely resolved, he was evaluated by 
cardiology, who recommended optimal medical management prior to 
surgery. His blood pressure baseline of 160s-170s was better 
controlled on increased lisinopril and the addition of Imdur. 
When a new SBP baseline of 110s-140s was established, the 
patient was cleared for surgery. 
.
#CCY: The patient underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy with 
general surgery. Intraoperatively, the patient was found to be 
bradycardic to ___ with a new suspected junctional rhythm 
(elaborated on further below).  The patient was stabilized and 
his heart rate returned to normal, and he was transferred to the 
floor for continued post-operative care. There were no other 
intraoperative complications. On the floor, he was maintained on 
IV fluids in the immediate post-operative period, during which 
time he experienced several bouts of nausea/vomiting x2 days. 
The patient's pain was well-controlled throughout this time. 
When the nausea/vomiting subsided, the patient's diet was 
advanced until he tolerated two full meals (regular diet), after 
which he was deemed stable for discharge.
.
#. HTN: The patient's blood pressure was poorly controlled on 
admission with baseline SBP in 150s-160s. With the addition of 
Imdur 60mg/day and an increased dose of Lisinopril (40mg/day to 
60mg/day), we achieved a new baseline SBP in 110s-140s. The 
patient's blood pressure is always higher on the day of 
hemodialysis, likely secondary to accumulated fluid retention 
over the days between HD sessions. The patient is to continue 
taking Imdur 60mg/day and Simvastatin 40mg/day at home. The 
patient was instructed to take only 40mg/day of Lisinopril 
(admission dose) at home.
.
#. EKG changes: The patient presented initially with ECG 
significant for a new incomplete RBBB pattern and TWI in V1-V3 
compared to priors. Following a bradycardic even 
intraoperatively, his ECG demonstrated diffuse TWI V2-V6 with 
apparent resolution of RBBB pattern. On POD#1, the new TWIs had 
resolved and the RBBB pattern re-appeared. ECG now same as on 
admission. The patient experienced no additional episodes 
related to ECG changes.
.
#. ESRD: The patient continued on hemodialysis per outpatient 
schedule on ___, and ___ throughout the 
admission period without event. Cinacalcet was held per renal 
secondary to hypocalcemia. Continued on other at-home meds, 
including calcium acetate and nephrocaps.
.  
#. DM2: Elevated BG on admission with AG of 17. Gap closed after 
IVF and insulin. At-home insulin doses and sliding scale were 
modified depending on patient's ability to eat. FSBG levels were 
followed throughout his admission without event.
.
#.CAD: Stable. The patient was continued on ASA, ACEi, and 
Simvastatin was increased to 40mg per cardiology 
recommendations.
.
#.HLD:  Stable. Continued on statin as above, as well as 
fenofibrate.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted to the ___ hospial because you were having 
abdominal pain similar to your previous episodes of 
pancreatitis. We gave you IV fluids and pain medication until 
your symptoms resolved. After 3 days of no eating or drinking, 
you were able to tolerate food/liquids without vomiting and your 
pain/nausea symptoms resolved. You missed your home dose of 
lantus in the morning and thus your blood sugars were high 
tonight. We gave you your lantus this evening and you should 
check your blood sugar before bed and treat it as you would for 
a blood sugar that is elevated prior to bedtime.  Please monitor 
your blood sugars carefully tomorrow and call your doctor if you 
have any questions.  Please take your lantus at lunch time 
tomorrow instead of at breakfast so you do not over dose 
yourself on insulin.

Your recurrent pancreatitis was attributed to gallstones, and so 
you were evaluated by the general surgeons, who recommended 
cholecystectomy (removal of your gall bladder). You were 
evaluated by the cardiologist, who suggested optimizing your 
blood pressure control prior to surgery. As a result, we 
increased your Lisinopril dose to 60mg/day and added Imdur 
(Isosorbide Mononitrate) 60mg/day. With these new medications, 
we achieved better control of your high blood pressure. 
Additionally, your simvastatin was increased to 40mg per day per 
cardiologist recommendations. You should continue taking the 
Imdur 60mg per day and simvastin 40mg per day as an outpatient. 
Please return to taking Lisinopril 40mg (NOT 60mg) per day as an 
outpatient. 

The general surgery team took you to the operating room, where 
you underwent a laparascopic (minimally invasive) 
cholecystectomy (gall bladder removal). During the 
intraoperative period, your heart rate slowed significantly and 
you developed a new cardiac arrhythmia (rhythm disturbance). The 
anesthesiologists were able to bring your heart rate back to 
normal and the new rhythm resolved without further incident. You 
recovered in the post-operative care unit in the immediate 
post-operative period and were transferred back to the internal 
medicine service for long-term recovery. 

While on the floor, you experienced minimal pain and 
nausea/vomiting, for which you were treated with additional pain 
and nausea medication. When your nausea subsided, you were able 
to tolerate fluids by mouth and your diet was advanced 
accordingly. You were discharged home with pain medication.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  History of pancreatitis and gallstones with acute onset right
upper quadrant pain, nausea, vomiting.

FINDINGS:  Ultrasound of the right upper quadrant demonstrates normal liver
echogenicity and contour.  No focal liver lesions are seen.  Several stones
are seen within the gallbladder fundus.  The gallbladder wall is thickened
measuring up to 7 mm and the gallbladder is moderately dilated.  A small
amount of ascites is seen.  No intrahepatic biliary dilation is seen.  The CBD
is not dilated measuring 3 mm.  The portal vein is patent with hepatopetal
flow.

There are bilateral pleural effusions, right greater than left.  The spleen is
not enlarged measuring 12 cm.  The pancreas is not visualized on this
examination.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Cholelithiasis, gallbladder wall thickening and moderate distention. 
Although cholecystitis is difficult to exclude on these appearances, these
appearances of gallbladder wall in the presence ascites may be due to third
spacing rather than inflammation.
2.  Small amount of ascites.
3.  Bilateral pleural effusions, right greater than left.

HISTORY:  Pre-operative.

FINDINGS:  In comparison with study of ___, there is continued enlargement of
the cardiac silhouette in a patient who has undergone a previous CABG
procedure and has intact midline sternal wires.  There is some increase in the
degree of right pleural effusion with continued atelectatic changes at the
base.  There is increased opacification along the lower right chest wall. 
This could represent some loculated component of the effusion.

No evidence of pulmonary vascular congestion.
